content.value_statement: Meeting transcripts often hide repeated communication patterns and missed coaching moments. This skill turns transcripts into structured feedback, examples, and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews meeting transcripts for behaviors such as conflict avoidance, interruptions, filler words, and active listening.
Calculates speaking ratios, turn lengths, and question patterns when speaker labels support the analysis.
Extracts specific examples with timestamps when transcript data includes timing information.
Suggests clearer alternative phrasing for difficult feedback and meeting facilitation moments.
Compares communication patterns across meetings, folders, or time periods.
Produces summaries with strengths, growth opportunities, statistics, and practical next steps.
limitations: Accuracy depends on transcript quality, speaker labels, timestamps, and available meeting context.
The skill cannot reliably analyze raw audio or video without a transcript.
It can infer communication patterns, but it cannot prove intent or emotion.
Sensitive transcripts should be kept local and reviewed before sharing outputs.

use_cases.title: Improve Leadership Communication
use_cases.description: Review team meeting transcripts to find patterns in facilitation, directness, listening, and action item clarity.

use_cases.title: Prepare Coaching Feedback
use_cases.description: Turn transcript evidence into constructive examples for coaching conversations, development plans, or performance reviews.

use_cases.title: Track Personal Growth
use_cases.description: Compare meetings across months or quarters to measure changes in interruptions, question quality, and filler word use.

prompt_templates.title: Find Key Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a broad first review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the meeting transcripts in this folder. Summarize my main communication patterns, strengths, and three areas to improve.

prompt_templates.title: Review Conflict Avoidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these transcripts for moments where I avoided direct feedback or difficult conversations. Include examples and better phrasing.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Facilitation Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my facilitation style across these two meeting folders. Focus on speaking ratio, questions asked, inclusion, and decision clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Build Development Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the last quarter of transcripts and create a communication development plan with trends, priority behaviors, examples, and measurable next steps.

output_examples.input: Analyze my team meetings for facilitation style.
output_examples.output: The report identifies speaking balance, question quality, disagreement handling, inclusion of quiet participants, and action item clarity. It includes examples and practical recommendations.

output_examples.input: Tell me when I avoided conflict in these transcripts.
output_examples.output: The analysis highlights indirect phrasing, hedging language, topic changes, and missed feedback moments. It suggests direct alternative wording for each example.

output_examples.input: Compare my meetings from Q1 and Q2.
output_examples.output: The comparison summarizes changes in interruptions, listening signals, filler words, and follow-up clarity. It separates improvements from remaining growth areas.

best_practices: Use transcripts with clear speaker names, dates, and timestamps for stronger evidence.
Ask about one communication behavior at a time when you need detailed coaching feedback.
Review sensitive examples before using them in performance reviews or shared coaching documents.
anti_patterns: Do not treat transcript analysis as proof of intent, emotion, or character.
Do not analyze private meetings without proper permission from participants.
Do not combine poor transcripts with broad judgments about communication quality.

faq.question: What file types can this skill work with?
faq.answer: The instructions mention text transcripts, Markdown, VTT, SRT, and document exports when the assistant can read them.

faq.question: Does it process audio recordings directly?
faq.answer: It is designed around transcript analysis. Raw audio or video usually needs transcription before reliable analysis.

faq.question: Can it calculate speaking ratios?
faq.answer: Yes, when the transcript has clear speaker labels and enough structure to estimate speaking turns or timing.

faq.question: Can it help with performance review preparation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can collect transcript-based examples, strengths, growth areas, and action-oriented feedback for review materials.

faq.question: How should sensitive meeting data be handled?
faq.answer: Keep transcripts local when possible, limit access, and remove confidential details before sharing reports.

faq.question: Does it replace a communication coach?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured evidence and suggestions, but human judgment is still needed for context and coaching decisions.
